name: AI GridWatch data center project tracker
caveat:
A working set of identified proposals a community can track, not a census — most of the country's activity is not in here yet.

**Each row carries its own provenance.** Rows showing a verification date link to reporting or the governing body's own record and were read on that date; rows marked *unverified* have no source on record — a lead to check, not a fact to cite.

**Stage is derived, not asserted.** *Hearing scheduled*, *Awaiting decision*, *Approved* and *Withdrawn* are computed from each row's milestone dates on every rebuild, so a hearing date that has passed stops reading 'scheduled'. Hearings get moved and projects re-file under new names — treat a scheduled date as the earliest to act by, and confirm with the clerk before relying on it. Leads are mined into data/project_candidates.json and promoted here only after a human reads a primary source.

schema.name: Project or code name.
schema.filing_llc: Shell LLC on the filing (ties to the campus registry), or blank.
schema.locality: Town or county the project sits in.
schema.size_mw: Planned IT/critical load in MW, or blank.
schema.announced: ISO date first publicly proposed, or blank.
schema.rezoning_filed: ISO date the rezoning/permit application was filed, or blank.
schema.hearing_date: ISO date of the next/decisive public hearing, or blank.
schema.decided_date: ISO date a terminal decision was reached, or blank.
schema.outcome: approved | denied | withdrawn | blank (blank = still live).
schema.stage: DERIVED status shown on the page (Hearing scheduled, Awaiting decision, In review, Proposed, Rumored, Approved, Denied, Withdrawn).
schema.days_to_hearing: DERIVED days until the hearing (negative once past), or blank.
schema.source: Primary URL backing the current status.
schema.as_of: ISO date the source was read, or blank.
schema.verified: true if a source is on record.

projects.name: PW Digital Gateway
projects.note: Approved in 2023 (4-3-1) but the rezoning was judicially voided over defective hearing notice; county and developer dropped their appeals in 2026, ending the project as approved.

events.summary: Prince William Board of Supervisors approved the rezoning 4-3-1 after a ~27-hour public hearing - roughly 2,100 acres / 23M sq ft along Pageland Lane, billed as the world's largest data center corridor.
Virginia's Court of Appeals upheld a lower-court ruling voiding the rezoning over defective public-hearing notice (March 2026).
County dropped its legal appeals (~$1.7M spent defending the project) and the developer withdrew, terminating the approved Digital Gateway (April 2026).

projects.name: Plaza 500 (Lincolnia)
projects.note: By-right data center on the 34-acre 6299 Edsall Road site; the required substation faces a Fairfax County Planning Commission Public Facilities (2232) review on Sept 24, 2026 amid organized opposition.

events.summary: Starwood Capital filed permit applications and building plans for Plaza 500 South, the first of two data center buildings on the 34-acre 6299 Edsall Road site (by-right, no rezoning hearing required).
Rep. Don Beyer, Alexandria's mayor and city council, and residents pressed Fairfax County to deny the substation that would power the campus - proposed within ~100 ft of homes.
Fairfax County Planning Commission Public Facilities (2232) review of the Edsall Road substation, 7 p.m. - the decisive vote residents can weigh in on.

projects.name: Project Iron Spur
projects.note: ~129-acre hyperscale campus proposed across from Rural Hall town hall; Forsyth County Planning Board recommended denial. Commissioners held the public hearing July 30, 2026 - decision pending.

events.summary: Forsyth County Planning Board recommended denial, citing scale and intensity that 'could result in significant offsite impacts to nearby residents.' Rural Hall town officials reversed their opposition after a tax-revenue annexation offer.
County commissioners held the public hearing on the rezoning after months of resident opposition; a final decision was pending as of this record.

projects.name: Meta Hyperion
projects.note: Approved and under construction - a ~5 GW, ~$27B campus. Louisiana approved new Entergy natural-gas generation to serve it; ratepayer cost allocation is the live fight, not the siting.

events.summary: Campus scaled to ~5 GW and ~$27B (up from an announced $10B); Entergy's plan for ten new gas units to serve it advanced through the Louisiana PSC (early 2026).

projects.name: Burkhalter Road data center (4AM Development)
projects.note: Two-story 230,000 sq ft data center plus a 32,000 sq ft substation on ~26.5 acres at 6539 Burkhalter Road (R-4 residential to Office & Business rezoning). Planning Commission recommended approval 5-1; City Council decides Aug 18, 2026. Bulloch County, separately, has been extending data-center moratoriums.

events.summary: Statesboro Planning Commission voted 5-1 to recommend approval of 4AM Development LLC's rezoning of ~26.5 acres at 6539 Burkhalter Road (chair dissenting), with a condition dedicating a 10-ft frontage strip for future road work.
Statesboro City Council scheduled to consider the rezoning request - the decisive vote.

projects.name: West Erwin Street data center (Barrio Resources)
projects.note: Special use permit for a bitcoin-mining data center on ~1.92 acres near downtown (W. Erwin St & N. Ross Ave) denied 5-2 by the Planning & Zoning Commission - staff found it inconsistent with the Future Land Use Map and comprehensive plan, after resident opposition over water, noise, and proximity to homes. Applicant may appeal.

events.summary: Tyler P&Z denied the special use permit 5-2. Planning staff: 'inconsistent with the Future Land Use Map and the Tyler Tomorrow Comprehensive Plan.' Residents cited water use, noise, and proximity to surrounding homes.

projects.name: Aligned Data Centers - Pataskala industrial park
projects.note: 200 MW campus in three buildings on ~89 acres at Broad St SW & Mink St SW. Planning & Zoning recommended rejection 5-2 after protests filled City Hall; City Council decides Aug 25, 2026 (5:30 p.m.). Council has separately advanced a ballot measure that could ban large data centers.

events.summary: Pataskala Planning & Zoning Commission voted 5-2 to recommend that City Council reject Aligned's site plan, hours after residents rallied on the City Hall lawn.
Pataskala City Council public hearing on the site plan, 5:30 p.m., council chambers - the decisive vote.

projects.name: King of Prussia campus (MLP Ventures)
projects.note: Five-site, 4.6M sq ft campus across King of Prussia. Applications were filed in early March 2026, roughly ten days before Upper Merion's new data-center ordinance took effect - exempting them from its residential buffer, noise, and water-use rules. The township Planning Commission voted against three of the proposals in July 2026; review continues amid packed hearings and organized opposition.

events.summary: Applications filed in early March 2026, ~10 days before Upper Merion's new data-center ordinance took effect - grandfathering the projects out of its residential buffer, noise, and water-use requirements.
The 4.6M sq ft, five-site plan by MLP Ventures was publicly unveiled; neighbor pushback began immediately.
In July 2026 the Upper Merion Planning Commission voted against three of the data-center proposals; hundreds of residents packed hearings in opposition. Township review continues.

projects.name: AWS Calvert Technology Center
projects.note: Eight data center buildings (266,000-332,000 sq ft each) proposed at 1650 Calvert Cliffs Parkway on Constellation-owned parcels near the Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant. AWS formally withdrew the concept site plan on Aug 4, 2026 - after first-round county review comments and before any resubmission. Timeline documented on the county's own project page.

events.summary: Amazon Data Services Inc. submitted initial site plan documents; the application was formally accepted for processing May 27, 2026.
County agencies completed first-round review of the concept site plan and returned comments to AWS.
AWS formally withdrew the Calvert Technology Center concept site plan application, per the county's project page, without resubmitting a revised plan.

projects.name: xAI Colossus
projects.note: Operating and expanding (~$20B, ~2 GW ambition). The live fight is air quality: on-site gas turbines in southwest Memphis - an area already failing federal ozone standards - drew a Clean Air Act suit. Environmental groups' tracking put unpermitted turbines at 27 in Feb 2026, growing to 59 by mid-2026 across the Colossus complex (incl. Colossus 2 in Southaven, MS).

events.summary: In July 2025, after SELC threatened a citizen suit, the Shelby County Health Department issued an air permit covering 15 of the 30+ turbines then operating unpermitted at the Memphis site.
NAACP, represented by Earthjustice and SELC, filed a Clean Air Act suit against xAI and MZX Tech (N.D. Miss.) over unpermitted gas turbines serving the Colossus complex.

projects.name: Nordson campus data center (Cervenka)
projects.note: Use variance to convert three newer buildings on the longtime Nordson Corporation campus into a data center complex - denied by the Board of Zoning Appeals on July 30, 2026, less than 24 hours after a hearing where 100+ residents packed City Hall and spilled onto the lawn. The developer's remaining path is an appeal in Lorain County Common Pleas Court.

events.summary: Amherst Board of Zoning Appeals denied the use variance, releasing its decision less than 24 hours after a packed hearing (100+ residents, capacity limits pushed the crowd outside).

projects.name: Hexa Builders data center (Black Horse Pike)
projects.note: Previously-approved warehouse project at 3043 South Black Horse Pike amended in early April 2026 to include a 1,000,000 sq ft data center. Two weeks later the township council stripped data-center permissions from the site and banned data centers township-wide; the planning board then deemed the amended application incomplete. Hexa is now suing the township for $300M+. Not dead - the litigation decides it.

events.summary: Hexa Builders filed an amended application in early April 2026 converting one approved warehouse into a 1M sq ft data center at 3043 South Black Horse Pike.
Township council passed two ordinances: one stripping data-center permissions from the specific site, the other banning data centers township-wide.
Planning board unanimously deemed the amended site-plan application incomplete - blocking the project without rejecting it on the merits.
Hexa Builders sued Monroe Township for more than $300 million in damages over the ban and the completeness review.

projects.name: Project Taurus (Raeden)
projects.note: Retrofit of an existing building on Garden of the Gods Road into the city's first AI data center, by California-based Raeden. Administratively approved by city staff in June 2026; the planning commission denied residents' appeals after a marathon hearing; two new appeals now send it to City Council, whose hearing must fall between Aug 29 and Sept 28 (likely mid-September - date not yet set). Chelsea Glen neighbors cite power, water, and noise from a prior Bitcoin operation at the site.

events.summary: City planning department administratively approved the Project Taurus application in June 2026; neighbors immediately announced an appeal.
Five appeals - including one from Chelsea Glen residents and the transparency group Integrity Matters - met the city's requirements to proceed.
Planning Commission denied the citizens' appeals after a ~14-hour hearing, upholding the approval 6-2.
Two new appeals filed, sending the decision to City Council - the final local authority. Hearing must occur between Aug 29 and Sept 28, 2026.

projects.name: Deep Green downtown data center
projects.note: 24 MW data center plus a 16 MW fuel-cell plant on 2.5 acres near the Grand River downtown, with a closed-loop water-glycol cooling system (~500,000 gal/yr). The Planning Commission recommended the rezoning 5-2 in March 2026, but Deep Green withdrew its rezoning request on April 6, 2026, ending the proposal before a council vote.

events.summary: Lansing City Planning Commission voted 5-2 to recommend the rezoning for the 24 MW data center + 16 MW fuel-cell plant.
Deep Green withdrew its rezoning application, axing the downtown proposal before City Council voted.

projects.name: Stargate Abilene
projects.note: The flagship Stargate site, built by Crusoe on Lancium's Clean Campus - the most complete Stargate location, with roughly four of eight buildings operational (~0.3 GW live) as of mid-2026. OpenAI and Oracle capped the site at 1.2 GW in March 2026, dropping further expansion amid grid-interconnection delays exceeding a year. Power is a mix of on-site natural gas and grid supply.

events.summary: In March 2026 OpenAI and Oracle capped the Abilene site at 1.2 GW, dropping expansion plans amid grid delays of more than a year; later buildings have run behind their permitted schedules.

projects.name: EdgeCore Shannon Hill campus
projects.note: 697 acres purchased in the Shannon Hill Regional Business Park for a 3.9M sq ft, 1.1+ GW campus - a $17B+ investment announced June 2025, phased over several years. No construction start date or tenants disclosed at announcement. Part of a data-center surge in a small county that already hosts an AWS campus.

events.summary: EdgeCore announced the land purchase (697 ac, Shannon Hill Regional Business Park) and $17B+ phased campus plan in June 2025; construction timing and tenants undisclosed.

projects.name: Google West Texas campuses
projects.note: Part of Google's $40B Texas investment through 2027: AI data-center campuses in Haskell County (one paired with a new Intersect/TPG solar + battery storage plant) and Armstrong County, plus additional sites in Pampa and Wilbarger Counties. Company-owned and proceeding, not a contested local rezoning.

events.summary: Google announced a $40B Texas investment through 2027, including AI data-center hubs in Haskell and Armstrong Counties.

projects.name: Augusta Township data center (Thor Equities)
projects.note: The township board rezoned 500+ acres of farmland near Milan from agricultural to general industrial for a hyperscale data center by NY-based Thor Equities. Residents petitioned the decision onto the ballot and voters overturned the rezoning 89.5%-10.4% on Aug 4, 2026 — a rare referendum defeat of an already-approved data-center rezoning.

events.summary: Voters overturned the industrial rezoning 89.5% to 10.4%, blocking the Thor Equities data center.

projects.name: Astra data center campus (Digital Realty)
projects.note: Digital Realty bought ~1,435 acres in the Astra Enterprise Park (the former Sunflower Army Ammunition Plant) to develop a ~600 MW campus across Astra North and South; first phase ~$4B excluding equipment, customer undisclosed. The second major data center proposed near the $4B Panasonic battery plant.

events.summary: Digital Realty unveiled preliminary plans for a ~600 MW, ~1,435-acre campus at Astra Enterprise Park near the Panasonic battery plant.
